item.title: Album of the Week – Ciarán Ryan ‘Kick Up The Dust’
item.description: This is the third solo album from renowned banjo player, CIARÁN RYAN and, as the title suggests, it’s a full-on, thrilling musical jamboree. Ciarán – founder member of world-folk band Dallahan – is rooted in Irish traditional music but he doesn’t stop there as bluegrass, funk and rock are fused boldly into the tracks […]

item.title: Album of the Week – Elgin And The Marbles ‘The Sun Never Sets’
item.description: This punchy debut album by Glasgow’s newest indie-folk storytellers ELGIN AND THE MARBLES is described as “a semi-concept album” outlining the last decade of Britain. The band is fronted by Callum Baird, a Glasgow-based songwriter, who was editor of The National for seven years and is now editor-in-chief of a publishing group that includes […]

item.title: Win MacDonald Bros Show Tickets
item.description: The MacDonald Bros – one of Scotland’s busiest and best known duos – are bringing their fabulous Sound of Scotland show to the Beacon Arts Centre Greenock on Friday 10th April. item.title: Album of the Week – Kris Drever ‘Doing This For Love’
item.description: This album from the multi-award winning Scottish contemporary folk musician and songwriter, KRIS DREVER was ‘made with love for anyone who labours for love.’ These are the Orkney-born, Glasgow-based artist’s own words for a ten-strong collection of songs started during covid and finished in the studio in September last year. item.title: Guest – Heather Cartwright
item.description: Glasgow-based folk/trad musician, HEATHER CARTWRIGHT is the guest of Ian Oliphant on today’s edition of his Lunchtime Selection show. Heather recently released her version of the Robert Burns’ song “Sweet Afton.” She has won praise for her virtuosic fingerstyle and flat-picked guitar playing that provides a vibrant backdrop to her well-crafted, self-penned songs and interpretations […]

item.title: Album of the Week – John Graham & Jim Jack ‘Blackadder Water’
item.description: John Graham and Jim Jack have been a welcome part of the folk scene for decades and this is reflected in this excellent collection of songs that are rooted in the tradition that shaped them. The album, named after the river that winds through the Borders, reflects to great effect their connection to place […]

item.description: Eric Faulkner, best known as the charismatic guitarist of The Bay City Rollers, has reinvented himself as a thoughtful and passionate solo artist. item.title: Station Extends DAB Coverage
item.description: Celtic Music Radio has extended its DAB services with coverage now available across North Ayrshire and West Renfrewshire. The development in digital capacity is a boost to listeners across coastal and inland communities. item.title: Keep Celtic Music Radio On Air — For the Next 20 Years
item.description: For 20 years, Celtic Music Radio has broadcast Celtic music to listeners across Scotland and around the world. Behind the scenes, our studio equipment is more than 40 years old and now beyond repair. Replacement parts aren’t made anymore, and technical failures are happening daily. item.title: Album of the Week – Hot Tamale ‘Bringing The Light’
item.description: Long established acoustic duo from Tallahassee, Florida, HOT TAMALE create a warm blend of folk, blues, Americana, and roots music. Adrian Fogelin and Craig Reeder have always had a gift for making music that feels lived in and close to the bone and this, as well as their political and environmental activism, is very much in evidence on this release. item.title: Album of the Week – Sean Taylor ‘First Light’
item.description: SEAN TAYLOR is a unique songwriter rightly praised for delivering compelling music. This latest album from the talented troubadour is thoughtful and full of sincerity, and he delivers the 13 tracks with a voice that is a cross between John Martyn and Van Morrison. item.title: Album of the Week – RANT ‘Live In Glasgow’
item.description: This vibrant offering is the fifth album from Scotland’s chamber-folk quartet RANT, recorded live at Cottiers Theatre in Glasgow in September last year. It demonstrates effectively their widely-recognised, energising fiddle performances that are fully charged with tradition and finesse. item.title: Album of the Week – Isla Ratcliff ‘The Scottish Four Seasons’
item.description: Fiddle player, singer and composer, ISLA RATCLIFF’s second album, ‘The Scottish Four Seasons’, is a Scottish trad reinterpretation of Italian composer, Vivaldi’s famous work.
